# Way of Life - Habit Tracker (App Store ID 393159800) — Full Review Analysis

**Way of Life ApS · `com.larsparendt.wayoflife` · Health & Fitness, Productivity · free download with a 3-item free tier; premium sold as a one-time unlock for most of its history and as a subscription from 2023**

Every one of the **7,764 reviews** in `reviews.jsonl` was read individually, in its original language, and hand-coded. Nothing was sampled, keyword-filtered or skipped. Corpus: **2010-11-08 → 2026-09-06** (nearly 16 years), **83 storefronts**, **27 languages** (English 5,344, Chinese 538, Russian 466, Korean 263, Japanese 251, German 179, Spanish 144, Portuguese 133, and 19 more), corpus mean **4.62★**.

---

## How to read this

- Every quantified claim carries **count, percentage, denominator, scope, period, signal band and review IDs**. Signal bands are those in `GENERALIZED_STORE_REVIEW_ANALYSIS_PROMPT.md`.
- Theme counts are **non-exclusive**: a review carrying five ideas is counted in five themes. Percentages are *shares of reviews mentioning a thing* and sum past 100%.
- **§10 is a complete per-review index.** Any number here resolves to exact reviews; any review resolves to the findings it supports via §9.J.
- Review IDs appear as `` `366961974` `` (the `review_id` in `reviews.jsonl`) and as `#1` (position in date order, 1…7,764). Both appear in §10.
- Quotations are verbatim and short. Non-English text is quoted in the original with a translation. `…` marks an elision.
- Global percentages use **all 7,764 reviews**, from every storefront.

### ⚠️ Seven warnings before any number here is used

1. **This is a praise corpus.** 5★ 5,900 (75.99%), 1–2★ 285 (3.67%). Any-praise reviews are 81.88%. Complaints are few in absolute terms, so a *Meaningful* complaint (1–3%) here is dozens of reviews, not hundreds. Bands are computed on 7,764 and must be read with that in mind.
2. **Sixteen years, several products.** The app was a one-time $4.99 unlock with ads in the free version (ad complaints 2011-11-20 → 2020-01-15, the last a 2020-01 bundle promotion shown to paying users), added a tip jar (2018-11) and themes (2019-07), then moved premium to a subscription (first objection 2023-05-19). Themes are dated; §7 separates the eras. E6 (the subscription era) has only 906 reviews.
3. **Rating bursts.** 20 days carry 20 or more reviews (520 reviews, 6.70%); they are almost entirely 5★ and follow app updates or in-app rating prompts (§9.H). Authenticity marks of a coordinated campaign are absent: no generated-looking author names, 2 duplicate-body groups. §7.6 recomputes the headlines without the burst days.
4. **Short reviews.** 1,777 bodies (22.89%) have 30 characters or fewer; many are coded `PR_GENERIC` only. `NOISE` 71 reviews carry no usable content.
5. **Storefront is not language.** 82 of the 480 Russian-storefront reviews and 63 of the 210 German-storefront reviews are in English; Russian is also written from ua and kz (§6.26).
6. **Star and text sometimes disagree.** `CONTRA_RATING` **47** reviews, **0.61%** of 7,764; they are coded by their text (§4.3).
7. **Codes are hand judgement.** Each line in the classification file quotes the text behind its codes (§1.4); nothing was assigned by keyword or model. Outcomes and purchases are self-reported.

# PART 0 — READ THIS FIRST

The eight findings that should change a decision.

## 0.1 Simplicity is the product, and long-term users say so explicitly

`U_PRAISE_ANY` **6357** reviews, **81.88%** of 7,764 — High-priority signal, mean 4.80★, 2010-11-08 → 2026-09-06. The single largest reason is simplicity: `U_SIMPLICITY` **1682** reviews, **21.66%** of 7,764 — High-priority signal (`PR_SIMPLE` **1532** reviews, **19.73%** of 7,764; `PR_EASY` **1359** reviews, **17.50%** of 7,764; `PR_FAST` **197** reviews, **2.54%** of 7,764). The next is the at-a-glance picture: `PR_INSIGHTS` **838** reviews, **10.79%** of 7,764. Users describe the mechanism — a grid of green/red/grey cells, three states (yes, no, skip), habits that can be good or bad — as the thing other trackers lack: `PR_BETTER_THAN` **428** reviews, **5.51%** of 7,764; `PR_YESNO` **73** reviews, **0.94%** of 7,764; `PR_SKIP` **99** reviews, **1.28%** of 7,764.

Asking the developer *not* to add features is recent: `PR_KEEP_SIMPLE` **64** reviews, **0.82%** of 7,764, 61 of them in E5–E6. E6 reviewers include many long-term users: `TENURE_LONG` is 187 of 906 E6 reviews (20.6%), against 2.1% in E2.

> "I’ve possibly tried every habit app, and keep coming back to this one" — #6339, `7243490138`, us, 5★

> "nämlich drei Optionen anzubieten: erledigt, nicht erledigt, übersprungen" — #7439, `13769488285`, de, 5★
> *(translation: namely to offer three options: done, not done, skipped)*

> "Product Managers should study this app" — #7491, `13775690190`, us, 5★

> "Please do not change a single thing" — #6164, `6379998517`, de, 5★

#6339 is the most-voted review in the corpus (20 votes, 2021).

**Evidence:** `371487225`, `706035312`, `920087566`, `1144018930`, `1327138625`, `1447657510`, `3334514465`, `6745052457`, `11023850234`, `14502250642`.

## 0.2 The one structural request for fifteen years: habits that are not daily yes/no

`U_FLEX_REQ` **347** reviews, **4.47%** of 7,764 — Very strong signal, mean 4.13★, 2011-08-14 → 2026-06-03. It combines `REQ_FREQUENCY` **214** reviews, **2.76%** of 7,764 (specific weekdays, N times a week, weekly or monthly goals), `REQ_COUNT` **129** reviews, **1.66%** of 7,764 (quantities, several times a day) and `NEG_YESNO` **36** reviews, **0.46%** of 7,764 (a partial or 'yellow' state). It is the most frequent code in 4★ reviews after generic praise (§4.2): 96 of 1,281 4★ reviews ask for frequency.

The request appears in 15 of the 16 calendar years 2011–2026. Users work around it with skip, which then distorts the percentages they value (`NEG_CHART` 38); a reviewer in 2016 was already waiting for "promised weekly/monthly options" (#4129).

> "缺少频次的选择" — #5130, `1804926052`, cn, 5★
> *(translation: frequency choice is missing)*

#5130 (2017, cn) is one of the most-voted reviews (6 votes).

## 0.3 The one-time unlock: praised as fair by buyers, resisted at $4.99 by non-buyers, especially in China

Before the subscription era premium was a one-time purchase ("$4.99", "30块" in China) over a free version limited to three items. Buyers state it was worth it: `MON_VALUE` **342** reviews, **4.40%** of 7,764 — Very strong signal, mean 4.90★, 2011-06-24 → 2026-06-20. Non-buyers object: `U_PRICE_OBJECTION` **579** reviews, **7.46%** of 7,764 — High-priority signal, mean 3.58★, 2011-05-21 → 2026-07-14, led by `MON_PRICE` **306** reviews, **3.94%** of 7,764 and `MON_FREE_LIMIT` **250** reviews, **3.22%** of 7,764.

The objection peaked when the app was young and the free tier had ads: `MON_PRICE` 6.7% of E2 and 6.5% of E3, against 1.6% of E5. China carries 82 of the 306 price objections (26.8%), and price is 15.5% of cn reviews; several name the price at which they would buy (12 yuan). The three-item limit was not always clear before download: `MON_DISCLOSURE` **33** reviews, **0.43%** of 7,764.

## 0.4 The move to a subscription broke a promise to lifetime buyers

`MON_SUBSCRIPTION` **40** reviews, **0.52%** of 7,764 — Emerging signal, mean 2.70★, 2023-05-19 → 2026-06-08. All 40 are in E6, where they are **4.42% of 906 E6 reviews** (segment rate, Very strong within the era) and 15 of the 181 1★ reviews in the corpus. Purchases that fail to restore rise with it: `BUG_PURCHASE` 14 of 906 E6 reviews (1.55%), against 0.91% in E5.

Three distinct complaints sit under the code: lifetime buyers told they no longer have premium; new users who expected the one-time price that older reviews describe; and prices that differ between weeks, platforms or regions.

## 0.5 Local-only data: loved for privacy, lost on updates and new phones

`U_DATA_RISK` **123** reviews, **1.58%** of 7,764 — Meaningful signal, mean 3.04★, 2011-12-11 → 2026-06-18: `BUG_DATA_LOSS` **38** reviews, **0.49%** of 7,764, `NEG_BACKUP_MANUAL` **13** reviews, **0.17%** of 7,764, `BUG_BACKUP` **10** reviews, **0.13%** of 7,764, `NEG_DROPBOX_BLOCKED` **18** reviews, **0.23%** of 7,764. The same design is praised by others: `PR_PRIVACY` **12** reviews, **0.15%** of 7,764.

## 0.6 Two update failures account for most breakage; crash waves arrive within days

`U_UPDATE_REGRESSION` **84** reviews, **1.08%** of 7,764 — Meaningful signal, mean 3.08★, 2011-11-05 → 2026-02-22. `BUG_UPDATE_BROKE` **54** reviews, **0.70%** of 7,764 — Emerging signal, mean 2.80★, 2012-05-18 → 2025-12-26. 21 of the 54 are from 2012-11/12 (a release that left the app unusable or corrupted data for some users) and 12 from 2016-05/06 (the app crashed on "updating journal" at launch; reviews arrived from mx, ru, se, au, cn and us within two days). On the Chinese storefront, 11 reviews in 2015-01-23 → 2015-01-30 report the app crashing immediately after buying premium ("钱扣了就开始闪退，无限闪退" *(the money was taken and it started crashing, endlessly)* (#2797, `1134555630`, cn, 1★)). Smaller clusters: a 2014-06 redesign that some reviewers called awful and greedy (`NEG_UPDATE_WORSE` 17), a 2017-07 release that wiped some histories, and the 2023 removal of the old Today widget (`NEG_LOST_FEATURE` 7).

## 0.8 Five-star bursts follow updates and rating prompts; they are not a campaign

20 days carry 20+ reviews: 2026-04-22 (41), 2015-02-08 (34), 2025-06-05 (32), 2016-03-02 (30), 2026-02-20 (30), 2023-04-04 (29), 2012-11-19 (28), 2016-03-18 (28), and 12 more. They hold 520 reviews (6.70%), 86.15% of them 5★. Reviewers name the trigger: `REV_SOLICITED` **18** reviews, **0.23%** of 7,764 — Weak signal, mean 4.06★, 2012-08-16 → 2018-12-09, 7 of them between 2015-10 and 2016-03. The 2025–2026 bursts lean to long-term users (`TENURE_LONG` 65 of 200 burst reviews in those years).

> "they requested that I provide a review" — #3872, `1341572559`, us, 5★

> "Quit bugging me with review me review me crap" — #1338, `760754071`, us, 1★

> "app solicited a review 3 days in, after I paid for the premium version" — #3668, `1313359649`, us, 4★


No marks of a coordinated campaign were found: no generated-looking author names, 2 duplicate-body groups (5 short generic reviews), and 26 cross-storefront authors who are long-term users reviewing again years apart (§9.H). The bursts inflate praise shares modestly; §7.6 shows the headlines hold without them.

**Evidence:** `693544347`, `1143627439`, `1263625007`, `1341728315`, `1386751704`, `9786428862`, `12736964969`, `13771165190`, `13983453032`, `13989977933`.

# PART 1 — SCOPE AND METHOD

## 1.1 Files used

| `app store review/76. Way of Life - Habit Tracker - Build a better, stronger you/reviews.jsonl` | **the corpus**; every claim resolves here | 7,764 |
| `by_country/*.jsonl` | 83 per-storefront files | 7,764 (union) |

## 1.2 Schema actually present

All 13 fields are present on all 7,764 records; no title or body is empty.

| Field | Used for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `review_id` | primary key | 7,764 distinct; zero duplicates |
| `country`, `country_name` | §6 | 83 storefronts |
| `rating` | §4 | integers 1–5 only |
| `title`, `body` | **read in full for every record** | median body length 80 characters |
| `author` | authenticity tests only (§9.H) | 26 names appear on more than one storefront |
| `date` | §7 | 2010-11-08 → 2026-09-06 |
| `vote_count`, `vote_sum` | §9.H | 202 reviews have votes; max 20 |
| `is_edited` | §9.H | 163 edited |
| `app_id`, `app_name` | constant (`393159800`, `Way of Life - Habit Tracker`) | |

**Not present, and therefore never claimed:** app version per review, purchase or subscription records, developer responses, device, and any identifier linking a reviewer to a purchase.

**Reviews read: 7,764/7,764 = 100%. Reviews hand-coded: 7,764/7,764 = 100%.** No deduplication was applied: there are no technical duplicates. Identical bodies under different authors (5 reviews in 2 groups) are kept and disclosed (§9.H).

## 1.4 Processing method

1. `76-dump.py` emits all 7,764 reviews in date order with a stable index (1…7,764).
2. Reviews were read in date order in batches of 100 (78 classification files, the last holding 64), in full, in the original language. Translations quoted here were checked against the source string.
3. Each review received hand codes plus a note quoting the text that drove them (`76-cls/*.txt`, 7,764 lines).
4. **After every batch**, `76-check-cls.py` re-asserted each line's `review_id` at its index and that every quoted fragment in the note occurs in that review. Lines were written without IDs and `76-fill-ids.py` filled them from the index, so an ID cannot drift from its text (§9.C).
5. `76-build-classification.py` rejects unknown codes, adds mechanical codes (`STAR_n`, `ERA_En`) and derives 15 unions.
6. `76-validate.py` runs the data checks in §9.C.
7. `76-build-report.py` computes every number and chooses every representative ID from the data at build time. It **refuses to write** if any quotation is not found verbatim in the review it is attributed to, and asserts every trend direction stated in the narrative.
8. `76-verify-report.py` re-reads the written file and checks it against the corpus (§9.M).

**Classification is hand judgement, not an algorithm.** No clustering, keyword rule or model assigned a code.

## 1.5 Signal thresholds

| Share of reviews | Label |
|---|---|
| < 0.1% | Ignore by default |
| 0.1% – < 0.5% | Weak signal |
| 0.5% – < 1% | Emerging signal |
| 1% – < 3% | Meaningful signal |
| 3% – 5% | Very strong signal |
| > 5% | High-priority signal |

At n=7,764, 0.1% ≈ 8 reviews, 1% ≈ 78 and 5% ≈ 388. Segment rates (within a star band, era, storefront or the paid segment) are labelled as segment rates and show both denominators.

## 1.6 Limitations, stated plainly

- **Selection.** Satisfied users are prompted to rate (§0.8); dissatisfied users write when something breaks. Neither measures typical use.
- **Survivorship across 16 years.** People who abandoned the app early rarely return to review; E6 over-represents long-term users (`TENURE_LONG` on about a fifth of E6 reviews, §0.1).
- **Purchases are unverifiable.** Prices and restore failures are the reviewer's account.
- **No version data.** Product changes are dated from reviewer statements and clusters, and from the listing's current feature list.
- **Thin recent era.** E6 has 906 reviews; the subscription finding rests on 40 reviews.
- **Language mix.** 5,344 reviews are in English; 26 other languages carry 2,420.

# PART 2 — PRODUCT AND MONETIZATION MODEL

## 2.1 What the product is, from the reviews

A daily habit journal. The user lists items ("journals"), marks each day green (done), red (not done) or skip, optionally adds a note, and reads the result as bar and pie charts, trend lines and a weekly/monthly overview. Each item can be marked good or bad, so the colours invert for habits to avoid. From late 2015 the app counts chains (streaks). Reminders can be set; tags group items; data exports to CSV/Excel and backs up manually (Dropbox in the early years). A passcode or Face ID can lock it. The free version allows three items; premium unlocks unlimited items.

| Capability | Positive evidence | Friction evidence |

- Listing title **Way of Life - Habit Tracker**; seller **Way of Life ApS**; genres Health & Fitness, Productivity; age 4+; released 2010-11-07; current version **4.3.2**, dated **2026-04-20**; price Free; minimum iOS 15.6.

- The listing cites press including Tim Ferriss's podcast with Kevin Rose; reviewers name the same source (`MKT_PRESS`, §3.7). The listing text is the developer's and is not used as evidence.
- The public mean is above the corpus mean in 21 of 22 storefronts, by up to 0.38 (tw). Public counts include star-only ratings as well as written reviews; the corpus cannot say which kind drives the gap.

## 2.4 What could not be established

- The date premium became a subscription, and whether lifetime buyers were migrated automatically.
- Current prices by region; one reviewer saw $29 and then $99 in consecutive weeks of 2025 (#7322).
- Whether the rating prompts in 2025–2026 were in-app review requests or release-note appeals.
- How many users ever lost data; the corpus cannot give a rate.

**Why it works, in reviewers' words:**

- **Logging costs seconds, so it survives.** "almost 9 years since my last review and 13 since the first" (#7008, `10961979664`, ca, 5★); "I track 30+ items in under 2 minutes" (#5006, `1618497915`, de, 5★).
- **Honesty through colour.** "keeps me from fooling myself into thinking I did better than I really did" (#4815, `1501749022`, us, 5★); the red cell is the motivator: "I hate to break a winning steak" (#6230, `6656271875`, gb, 5★).
- **Good and bad habits in one grid.** "it reverses the red/green colours for yes and no" (#5215, `2033057159`, gb, 5★).
- **Skip without guilt.** "skip option for when you have days where you need to skip without breaking your chain" (#4543, `1430830624`, gb, 5★).
- **Chains (from 2015-11).** `PR_CHAINS` **129** reviews, **1.66%** of 7,764, 56 of them in E4: "Chains is going to change my life" (#3561, `1290249480`, gb, 5★).
- **The developer.** `PR_DEV` **268** reviews, **3.45%** of 7,764, rising from 2.1% of E1 to 6.7% of E6; reviewers name him and thank him for maintaining an app for over a decade: "Through steady updates, this continues to be the best habit/task tracking app out there for me." (#5659, `4420297480`, us, 5★)

The monetization story is told in §0.3, §0.4 and Part 5. Two further points: ads in the free version were the main 2013–2016 irritant and briefly appeared for paying users after the 2015-11 update ("Ads when already paid" (#3553, `1289364973`, us, 2★)); and paying twice across devices or accounts is reported 3 times ("you have to pay for each iPhone or iPad you use" (#1212, `741004355`, us, 1★)).

Returning users are reported alongside leavers: `CHURN_RETURN` 60 against `U_CHURN` 55. Reviewers who leave name data loss, price or the subscription; reviewers who return name the simplicity after trying heavier apps: "I just always end up coming back to the simplicity of Way of Life" (#7617, `13984329659`, gb, 5★).

Press and podcasts are the named acquisition source: `MKT_PRESS` **51** reviews, **0.66%** of 7,764 — Emerging signal, mean 4.94★, 2014-01-13 → 2026-02-23; 26 in E4, mainly Tim Ferriss's podcast with Kevin Rose and Ezra Klein's show ("Tim Ferriss Show podcast from Kevin Rose" (#3653, `1312703881`, us, 5★); "Thanks for the rec, Ezra Klein" (#4059, `1353940535`, us, 4★)), later *Atomic Habits* and, in Russia and Kazakhstan, Margulan Seisembay ("Спасибо Маргулану Сейсембаю" *(thanks to Margulan Seisembay)* (#5994, `5583547111`, ru, 5★)).

Through 2016 support is praised for speed ("developer emailed me back in less than 5 minutes" (#159, `504207844`, us, 5★); "innerhalb von einem Tag gelöst" *(solved within a day)* (#4359, `1390768771`, de, 5★)). Silence is reported from 2016 and is most frequent in E6 (9 of 20), alongside restore failures and a contact form that does not work ("secção de Contact no website não funciona" *(the Contact section on the website does not work)* (#7352, `13244707998`, pt, 1★)). Reviewers note the app is one developer: "I think they are just one person, so be patient" (#6536, `8458663871`, us, 5★).

## 4.3 Rating-versus-text contradictions

`CONTRA_RATING` **47** reviews, **0.61%** of 7,764. 29 are 4–5★ reviews whose text reports a problem (most frequent codes among them: `BUG_UPDATE_BROKE` 6, `BUG_DATA_LOSS` 6, `TENURE_LONG` 4, `MON_PRICE` 4): "DO NOT BUY UNTIL ITS FIXED" (#756, `694696960`, us, 4★); "it should have been free" (#6482, `7995883622`, in, 5★). 7 are 1–2★ reviews whose text is praise: "I absolutely love this app" (#7618, `13984571428`, au, 1★). The rest are 3★. All are kept and coded by their text.

**All contradiction IDs:** `588079580`, `694696960`, `695474794`, `751111942`, `784217425`, `932920375`, `1134206477`, `1388095978`, `1391137343`, `1392275425`, `1450394971`, `1450878966`, `1451520032`, `1455488507`, `1461832812`, `1488838993`, `1518613194`, `1520286682`, `1554882245`, `1638044822`, `1677344652`, `1756057326`, `2161516526`, `3284305026`, `3363437907`, `3513007843`, `3917044525`, `3986199179`, `4070891985`, `4454042434`, `4946701702`, `5063082574`, `7260949144`, `7518431458`, `7995883622`, `8883219703`, `10494068368`, `10928251512`, `10991727213`, `10993576781`, `12736188342`, `12746543382`, `13768754026`, `13811632248`, `13984571428`, `13987583857`, `14159487537`.

# PART 5 — PAID-USER AND UPGRADE ANALYSIS

## 5.1 The populations, and what they are not

- **Stated purchase: `MON_PAID` 349 (4.50% of 7,764)**, mean 4.29★, 2011-04-29 → 2026-04-25.
- **Stated purchase, refund or restore problem: `U_PAID` 388 (5.00%)**, mean 4.15★.
- **Intent to buy: `MON_INTENT` 93 (1.20%)**, mean 4.65★. **Worth it, without saying they bought: `MON_VALUE` not in `MON_PAID`** 278.
- **Upgrade barrier: `U_PRICE_OBJECTION` 579 (7.46%)**, mean 3.58★.

**None of these is a conversion rate.** The corpus cannot say how many users pay, renew or are refunded.

## 5.2 What triggers a purchase

Within the 349 reviews stating a purchase (segment rates):

1. **Hitting the three-item limit after the free version worked.** `PR_FREE` 26 (7.4%), `MON_BUY_ITEMS` 20 (5.7%), `MON_FREE_LIMIT` 7: "found myself wanting to add more and shelled out the $5" (#3959, `1346355361`, us, 5★); "bought the upgrade to have more than three lines to track" (#105, `485881908`, nz, 4★).
2. **The charts and the grid.** `PR_INSIGHTS` 50 (14.3%): "This is the only app I bought the paid version for, and I regret it not at all" (#4957, `1566334421`, us, 5★).
3. **Removing ads (to ~2018).** `NEG_ADS` 16 (4.6%): "Worth the upgrade to get rid of the ads" (#647, `670251014`, us, 5★).
4. **A press recommendation.** `MKT_PRESS` 6: "Used for one day then upgraded to the paid" (#3653, `1312703881`, us, 5★).
5. **Supporting the developer.** `MON_TIP` 15: "jumped at the chance to ‘tip’ the developers" (#5508, `3520578395`, au, 5★).

- **Paid, expected more**: "features missing that I would expect to see in a paid app" (#4822, `1505307158`, fr, 3★).
- **Paid, regretted**: "Ich würde die 5€ nicht nochmal für die App bezahlen" *(I would not pay the €5 for the app again)* (#4772, `1481286486`, de, 2★).

- **Three items is too few to evaluate**: "только купив поймете нужно ли оно вам" *(only by buying will you know if you need it)* (#6101, `6252563047`, ua, 2★); "This is not a Free app with in-app purchases. This is a $7 app" (#6456, `7749376108`, us, 1★).
- **Three items is a feature for some**: "forced me to prioritize the three most important tasks by paywalling more than 3" (#7013, `10969791376`, us, 5★).
- **A price they would pay**: "gladly pay .99 for an extra goal" (#3904, `1342032100`, us, 4★); "Купил бы полную версию если бы стоило хотя бы 200р" *(I would buy the full version if it cost 200 roubles)* (#6258, `6767712579`, ru, 5★).
- **Subscription refusal**: "I’m not paying a yearly subscription" (#7389, `13656328254`, us, 3★); "happy to pay up to £50 even for lifetime access" (#7539, `13795648107`, gb, 3★).
- **Discount timing**: "only offer a reduced price in the first days after installation" (#6304, `7054076524`, br, 5★).

## 5.6 Refund and churn drivers after purchase

`MON_REFUND` **9** reviews, **0.12%** of 7,764 — Weak signal, mean 1.89★, 2015-11-14 → 2025-09-11. The drivers are a purchase that did not work (`BUG_PURCHASE`), a subscription charge the reviewer did not expect (`MON_SUBSCRIPTION` + `MON_DISCLOSURE`), or a product that did not meet the price ("got my money back" (#4947, `1557935950`, ch, 1★)). Among purchasers, `U_CHURN` is 3 (0.9%).

## 5.7 What cannot be claimed here

- The share of users who buy premium, or how many lifetime buyers lost access in 2023–2026.
- Whether regional prices differ as reviewers report, or whether the $29 and $99 amounts are monthly, annual or lifetime.
- Whether refunds were granted.

## 6.25 High-spend and high-review-volume markets

**No consumer-spend dataset was fetched in this session**, so no spend ranking is asserted. Two groups are defined from captured sources:

- **High-spend proxy group** = the six eligible storefronts with the most public ratings in Apple's lookup API (an install-base proxy, not spend): us (5,247), ru (1,265), ca (768), de (709), gb (681), jp (673).
- **High-review-volume group** = storefronts with ≥200 reviews in this corpus: us, cn, ru, gb, ca, au, jp, kr, de.

| Group | Reviews | Mean ★ | Praise % | Price objection % | Flex request % | Platform request % | Data risk % | Subscription objection % | E6 share % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| High-spend proxy: us + ru + ca + de + gb + jp | 4,915 | 4.65 | 84.1% | 6.1% | 5.0% | 4.3% | 1.4% | 0.5% | 11.9% |
| High-volume: us + cn + ru + gb + ca + au + jp + kr + de | 6,019 | 4.64 | 82.2% | 7.7% | 4.7% | 4.3% | 1.6% | 0.5% | 10.5% |
| us only | 3,115 | 4.70 | 85.7% | 4.8% | 4.9% | 4.1% | 1.1% | 0.4% | 11.3% |
| cn + tw + jp + kr (East Asia) | 1,157 | 4.54 | 73.5% | 16.9% | 2.5% | 4.5% | 3.1% | 0.3% | 4.0% |
| ru + ua + kz (Russian-speaking) | 584 | 4.55 | 71.7% | 7.5% | 5.1% | 6.5% | 3.3% | 1.5% | 17.5% |
| de + dk + se + nl + ch + fr + es (continental Europe, eligible) | 786 | 4.56 | 83.8% | 7.9% | 6.2% | 3.6% | 1.3% | 0.5% | 17.0% |
| Global | 7,764 | 4.62 | 81.9% | 7.5% | 4.5% | 4.3% | 1.6% | 0.5% | 11.7% |

**Reading:** price objection is concentrated in East Asia, driven by China; the high-spend proxy group and the US sit below the global rate. The Russian-speaking group asks for other platforms and reports data risk at about 1.5–2× the global rate, and carries the highest subscription-objection share, though on few reviews. Continental Europe asks most for flexible frequency. Subscription objections are too few in any group to rank markets.

# PART 7 — TIME-TREND ANALYSIS

## 7.1 Method

Eras are cut at dated product changes that reviewers describe, checked against monthly volume and codes. §9.C asserts that dated events stay in their eras.

- **E1 → E2 at 2012-11-01**: the 2012-11 release that broke entry (`BUG_UPDATE_BROKE` cluster) and the first month above 140 reviews.
- **E2 → E3 at 2014-06-01**: version 3.0, a flat redesign that some reviewers called awful and greedy (`NEG_UPDATE_WORSE`), and the first China Dropbox complaints (2014-07).
- **E3 → E4 at 2015-11-01**: chains/streaks ship; ads briefly show to paying users.
- **E4 → E5 at 2018-01-01**: a calendar cut after the 2016–2017 update and data-loss clusters; reviews in this era see ads leave the free version (2018), the tip jar (2018-11), themes (2019-07) and Watch and widget requests replace iPad requests.
- **E5 → E6 at 2023-05-01**: the first subscription objection (2023-05-19).

## 7.4 What changed

**E1 (launch and paid unlock, 682 reviews, 4.51★).** A small, enthusiastic user base (praise 88.3%, the highest of any era) asking for the iPad (4.7%), frequency (4.5%) and quantities (2.9%). The price objection starts (5.7%).

**E2 (growth and the 2012-11 update, 1,452 reviews, 4.55★).** Monthly volume rises from 28 to 76. A release in 2012-11 breaks entry for many (21 breakage reviews in two months). Price objection peaks (6.7%); sync (2.8%), frequency and iPad lead requests, and per-habit reminders peak (1.9%).

**E3 (version 3, ads, China backup, 1,331 reviews, 4.60★).** A flat redesign divides users (`NEG_UPDATE_WORSE` 8 of 17). China becomes a major source (246 reviews) and cannot back up (`NEG_DROPBOX_BLOCKED` 16). The free-limit objection peaks (6.1%).

**E4 (chains and the podcast wave, 1,751 reviews, 4.66★).** Chains ship in 2015-11 and become praise (3.2%); press and podcasts bring users (26 of 51 `MKT_PRESS`); outcome statements peak (16.1%). The rating prompt draws most `REV_SOLICITED` (10 of 18). The 2016-05 crash wave hits (12 reviews).

**E5 (quiet years, 1,642 reviews, 4.67★).** Ads leave the free version (a 2020-01 bundle promotion to paying users draws 5 complaints), themes and a tip jar arrive, and requests move from iPad to Watch (1.8%) and widgets (1.3%). Price objection falls to its lowest (1.6%). Keep-it-simple praise appears (32).

**E6 (subscription era, 906 reviews, 4.70★).** The highest era mean, carried by veterans (`TENURE_LONG` 20.6%) and developer praise (6.7%), with bursts after 2025–2026 updates. Alongside: subscription objections (4.4%), restore failures (1.5%) and support silence (1.0%).

## 7.5 What persisted

- **Simplicity praise**, `PR_SIMPLE` in every era (17.0–22.5%), 2010-11-21 → 2026-09-02.
- **The frequency request**, `REQ_FREQUENCY` in every era (1.8–4.5%), 2011-08-14 → 2026-06-03.
- **The sync request**, `REQ_SYNC` in every era (0.9–2.8%), 2012-01-07 → 2026-05-07.
- **The three-item objection**, `MON_FREE_LIMIT` in every era (1.5–6.1%), 2011-05-21 → 2026-07-14.
- **Quantities**, `REQ_COUNT` in every era (0.8–2.9%), 2011-09-12 → 2026-03-24.

# PART 8 — PRODUCT IMPLICATIONS

Each item cites the findings it rests on. **Immediate fixes** address harms already reported; **experiments** test a hypothesis; **research questions** need data the corpus cannot give.

## 8.1 Immediate fix — honour every one-time and lifetime purchase (§0.4, §5.4)

- Restore premium for any App Store receipt of the old unlock, on any device, without a subscription prompt (`BUG_PURCHASE` 54, 14 in E6; `MON_SUBSCRIPTION` 40; #7316, #7572, #7550).
- Show a single, stable price per region and say on the paywall whether it is monthly, annual or lifetime (`MON_DISCLOSURE` 33; #7322).

## 8.2 Immediate fix — make data loss impossible by default (§0.5)

- Automatic, silent backup (iCloud) on by default, and a restore check before any update migrates data (`U_DATA_RISK` 123; `NEG_BACKUP_MANUAL` 13; #5114, #7384). The 4.3.0 note that Backup & Restore is free (external) addresses cost, not the default.

## 8.3 Immediate fix — a support route that answers (§3.8)

- A working in-app contact form, and an auto-reply with restore steps (`SUP_NONE` 20, 9 in E6; #7352, #4861).

## 8.4 Experiment — flexible frequency without losing the grid (§0.2)

- Let a journal be scheduled on weekdays or N times per week, with non-scheduled days rendered neutral and excluded from percentages. Hypothesis: converts the most common 4★ reason into 5★ and reduces skip-as-workaround (`U_FLEX_REQ` 347; `REQ_FREQUENCY` 96 of the 4★ reviews). Measure: star rating of reviewers who adopt it, skip usage.
- Test an optional count per day as a separate journal type, keeping yes/no as the default (`REQ_COUNT` 129; `NEG_YESNO` 36). Guard against the bloat users reject (`PR_KEEP_SIMPLE` 64).

## 8.5 Experiment — sync and a second device (§0.7)

- Ship iCloud sync to iPad before a Watch app. Hypothesis: sync is the paid feature reviewers say they would pay for (`REQ_SYNC` 139, #7564), and iPad is the second device most named (`REQ_IPAD` 123).

## 8.6 Experiment — a lifetime price alongside the subscription (§0.4, §5.5)

- Offer a lifetime option at a published price. Hypothesis: recovers the buyers who state a lifetime amount they would pay (#7539) without reducing subscription revenue from those who accept it (#7590). Measure: purchase mix and 1★ share among new users.

## 8.7 Experiment — prompt less, and never right after a purchase (§0.8)

- Suppress the rating prompt for 30 days after a purchase or a crash-free launch following a failure (`REV_SOLICITED` 18; #3668). Hypothesis: fewer resentful reviews with no loss of 5★ volume from veterans.

## 8.8 What the corpus says to keep

- The three-state grid, good/bad inversion and skip (§0.1).
- The charts and the at-a-glance overview (§3.2).
- A free tier that works for three habits — some users say the limit helps them focus (#7013, #4439).
- One-person, responsive development; reviewers thank it by name (§3.2).

## 8.9 Research questions the corpus cannot answer

1. How many lifetime buyers lost premium when the subscription launched, and how many restored it?
2. What share of active users have ever lost data, and on which path (update, new phone, reinstall)?
3. What proportion of users rely on skip to emulate weekly habits, and how does that distort their statistics?
4. Does the three-item free tier convert better or worse than a time-limited full trial?
5. How do veterans prompted after updates differ in retention from first-month users?

# PART 9 — EVIDENCE APPENDIX

## 9.A Counting rules

1. **Denominator.** Global = 7,764. Star band, era, storefront and purchaser denominators are stated at each use.
2. **Non-exclusive.** A review is counted once in each theme it carries. Percentages sum past 100%.
3. **Codes come from the text, never from the star rating.** A 5★ whose text is a complaint is coded as a complaint and flagged `CONTRA_RATING`.
4. **`MON_PAID` requires a statement of a purchase** (bought, upgraded, paid, premium user). `MON_VALUE` records a value judgement and does not by itself imply a purchase.
5. **`MON_SUBSCRIPTION` requires a subscription or a lost lifetime purchase in the text**; general price objections are `MON_PRICE`.
6. **`OUT_*` outcomes are first-person.** Anticipation is `JUST_STARTED`.
7. **Requests (`REQ_*`) are for capabilities absent at the time of the review**; a broken existing capability is `BUG_*`; a question about how something works is `MON_QUESTION`.
8. **Authenticity is never hand-coded.** Only textual evidence is coded (`REV_SOLICITED` when the text says the app asked for the review). Name, duplicate-body and burst marks are computed by rule (§9.H) and never used to drop reviews.
9. **Unions are derived, never hand-applied**; mechanical codes (`STAR_n`, `ERA_En`) come from the record.
10. **Signal bands** are computed from count ÷ denominator using §1.5.

## 9.C Validation — 1286 checks, 0 failures

`76-validate.py` output, verbatim:

```
1286 checks, 0 failures
  coverage: 7
  codes: 5
  theme_map: 669
  unions: 45
  mech: 13
  timeline: 8
  semantic: 536
  lang: 3
```

Coverage checks assert every index and ID; codes checks assert every code is defined and used; theme-map checks re-derive each code's review list; union and mechanical checks recompute them. Timeline checks: subscription objections never before E6; theme praise never before 2019; the tip jar never before 2018-06; China Dropbox complaints only 2014–2016; ad complaints end by 2020; the per-habit reminder request ends by 2019; the 2012-11/12 breakage cluster exists; rating-prompt complaints end by 2018. Semantic checks require every 1–2★ review to carry a negative, request, monetization, contradiction or noise code, every regret on a 5★ to be flagged as a contradiction, and `NOISE` lines to be short.

### What earlier runs caught

1. **Paraphrased quotations.** Notes quoting loosely were rewritten to the exact text, e.g. #5338 (the review spells "uptade"), #6536, #7156 ("to limited") and #7439 (word order).
2. **A wrong language tag**: #4647 was re-tagged from `ca` to `en`.
3. **Two over-strict semantic rules were removed rather than bending codes to fit**: "a purchase bug must be low-star" failed on 11 genuine 4–5★ reviews that also report a purchase problem (#527, #769, #2437, #2589, #2655, #3489, #3817, #3870, #5320, #6539, #6600); "a 5★ subscription mention must carry a contradiction" failed on 4 mild 5★ caveats (#6911, #7101, #7128, #7680).

### What validation cannot check

Whether a code is the *right* judgement. That is auditable only by reading the note on each line of `76-cls/`, which quotes the evidence.

They still inflate praise shares, which is why §7.6 removes them.

## 9.I Developer and support responsiveness — the evidence both ways

Developer replies are not in the dataset. Support praise: `PR_SUPPORT` **68** reviews, **0.88%** of 7,764 — Emerging signal, mean 4.79★, 2011-01-23 → 2026-03-23, e.g. "Fantastic response time by the team" (#4364, `1391078833`, gb, 5★). Developer praise: `PR_DEV` **268** reviews, **3.45%** of 7,764 — Very strong signal, mean 4.96★, 2011-01-13 → 2026-06-04. Support silence: `SUP_NONE` **20** reviews, **0.26%** of 7,764 — Weak signal, mean 2.05★, 2016-03-18 → 2026-01-23, e.g. "не восстанавливает покупку" *(does not restore the purchase)* (#7390, `13665885160`, us, 1★). Promises not kept: `NEG_DEV_PROMISE` **6** reviews, **0.08%** of 7,764 — Ignore by default, mean 3.00★, 2013-10-20 → 2026-03-21, e.g. "I asked the developer if he planned on expanding the maximum time 2 years ago" (#5260, `2653713386`, us, 3★). Both kinds continue into 2026.
